title: Task 6 shared-rule, response-expansion and slot-transform source trace
question: How do selected early-dispel macros, library merge rules and compiler/helper stages alter the compact source representation?

environment.description: Read-only HTTPS source inspection in memory; authored metadata and offline tests only.

versions.fingerprint: Per-file raw-byte SHA-256 recorded below; not an installed-stack fingerprint.

method.summary: Pinned in-memory source inspection: bounded seven-library extraction by Terra, lead verification and compiler/helper trace, independent review. No upstream program executed.
commands: Apply the PowerShell recipe in SCS-01-generation-pipeline.md with scs-shared-rules.evidence.json as the input record.
constraints: No game/save/lab access or upstream source/SSL/WeiDU execution.
No upstream source payload, effective script, or derived behavior fixture admitted.
This record covers the pinned Perl source pathway, not equivalence of the bundled Windows ssl.exe.
Only source facts and metadata checks; no policy simulation or runtime guarantee.

observations: The caller supplies an ordered library list; ordinary declarations append while replacement declarations reset the named body.
The SR SIAbjuration entry is an ordinary declaration containing only a comment, not a replacement; AvoidDispel is an ordinary extension.
Combine constructs target-selection probes before LastSeenBy-based action candidates in the inspected Perl source; final output is conditional on surviving action generation.
Low-script insertion can shift occupied slots or attempt merging, not simply write an empty slot.
counterevidence: The external-library comment does not account for later conditional freeaction-stun library append and final driver-supplied autolib.
A blank-looking ordinary declaration does not mean a prior protection test was removed.
No installed library list, autolib, actual compiler binary, or effective BCS was captured; source structure cannot identify an actual actor's behavior.

claims.statement: always.tph constructs an ordered library list, with conditional variants and external overrides; a later freeaction-stun append and driver-supplied autolib mean the external override is not unconditionally last.
limitations: Exact list is input-dependent; feature probes and generated/external libraries were not resolved against a game.
No guarantee of library order for arbitrary added call sites or later patches.

claims.statement: The pinned Perl reader appends ordinary TARGET/TRIGGER bodies and clears the body for *_REPLACE declarations; under base-then-SR loading the ordinary SIAbjuration comment does not clear the base test and AvoidDispel appends its extra conditions.
limitations: Static source reasoning only; comment stripping, subsequent substitutions and all selected libraries must be reflected in the final output.
No claim that ssl.exe was built from this Perl source.

claims.statement: The six selected early-dispel macro names resolve to bounded base-library definitions, with two ordinary SR extensions; no definitions of those names were found in the other five inspected variant libraries.
limitations: Seven-file negative search only; autolib, external libraries and weapon libraries were not searched for these names.
Engine predicate outcomes, invalid player slots and actual resource states remain unproved.

claims.statement: The inspected Perl source separates target/trigger expansion, Combine probes and subsequent LastSeenBy actions, explicit action weights, and OnContinue actions on a weighted continuation branch; candidate output is flushed only if an action survives.
limitations: Output-construction reasoning, not generated output or runtime observation.
Do not infer target-memory effects of See/False, observed probability, final first-dispel action choice, or fairness.
Complete action-definition/pruning and library inputs still require effective comparison.

claims.statement: When it allocates a missing script name, the mage generator calls upstream script stripping and low insertion; inspected helpers can clear recognized upstream slots, shift occupied slots and attempt a lower-script merge when full. An explicitly supplied script name bypasses that insertion block.
limitations: No effective CRE, slot restoration or merge_scripts result inspected.
The upstream naming rules are descriptive evidence, never this project's eligibility or removal policy.
